about.title: Personal Injury Help in Emeryville, California
about.longDescription: Emeryville sits at a busy crossroads of Alameda County, where I-80 traffic mixes with local trips along Powell Street, Hollis Street, and 40th Street. In the most recent full year on record, the city saw 135 injury collisions, 187 people hurt, and 3 traffic deaths — numbers that reflect just how much is happening on these roads every day, from commuters merging onto the freeway to shoppers crossing near the Bay Street area. If you were hurt in any kind of crash here, whether behind the wheel, on a bike, or on foot, the days afterward can feel overwhelming: medical visits, insurance calls, missed work. LawProactive exists to take one thing off your plate. We're a free service, not a law firm, that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney who can look at what happened and explain your options. There's no cost to talk with someone, and any attorney you're connected with works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your case results in a recovery. You don't have to figure this out alone or rush a decision while you're still healing.

whyChoose.title: Why People in Emeryville Reach Out to Us

items.title: Your Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity was involved. Waiting too long can mean losing your right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't Shut the Door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still pursue compensation. Your recovery is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in ordinary injury cases. That means your compensation isn't artificially limited just because your losses go beyond medical bills.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless They Win
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront fee to hire one. They only get paid if your case results in a settlement or verdict in your favor.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an accident in Emeryville?
items.answer: In most California personal injury cases, you have two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If a government agency or vehicle was involved, that deadline can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth checking your situation early rather than waiting.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, so being partly responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your total recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault, but you can still pursue a claim.

items.question: Are there certain times or areas where crashes are more commonly reported in Emeryville?
items.answer: Public crash records show collisions in Emeryville tend to cluster on Wednesdays between roughly 6 and 8 p.m., with corridors like I-80, Powell Street, Hollis Street, and 40th Street among the higher-volume locations for reported incidents. These are simply collision counts on record, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No. California does not cap non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in typical personal injury cases. This is different from some other states and can matter significantly in how a claim is valued.

items.question: Does it cost anything to use LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent attorney — we are not a law firm ourselves. Any attorney you're connected with works on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
